column3: “Weight” is rendered “encumbrance”; NASB supplies “let us also lay aside” and “us.”
“Looking to” is rendered “fixing our eyes on,” and “founder” “author”; “the faith” is rendered “faith.”
NASB follows the critical text (“against Himself”); “fainting in your souls” is rendered “lose heart.”
“Unto blood” is rendered “to the point of shedding blood.”
NASB supplies “you” and “when.”
“Whom” is rendered “those whom.”
NASB follows the critical text (“It is for discipline that you endure”); it supplies “as with.”
Close to the Greek.
“Fathers of our flesh” is rendered “earthly fathers,” and “correctors” “to discipline us.”
“During a few days” is rendered “for a short time,” and “benefitting” “good.”
“For those being present” is rendered “for the moment,” and “of grief” “sorrowful.”
“Lift up” is rendered “strengthen,” and “drooped … enfeebled” “weak … feeble.”
“The lame” is rendered “the limb which is lame,” and “disabled” “put out of joint.”
“Holiness” is rendered “sanctification,” and “behold” “see”; NASB supplies “men.”
“Observing” is rendered “See to it,” and “failing” “comes short.”
“Fornicator” is rendered “immoral,” and “profane” “godless.”
NASB adds “for” and renders “earnestly sought” as “sought.”
NASB includes “mountain,” which is in the Textus Receptus; “kindled with fire” is rendered “a blazing fire,” and “storm” “whirlwind.”
“A voice of declaration” is rendered “the sound of words,” and “excused themselves” “begged.”
NASB follows the critical text, without “or shot with an arrow.”
“The thing appearing” is rendered “the sight,” and “greatly afraid” “full of fear.”
NASB joins “to the general assembly” to verse 23.
NASB begins with “to the general assembly” and supplies “men.”
“Blood of sprinkling” is rendered “sprinkled blood”; NASB supplies “blood” after “than the.”
“Divinely instructing” is rendered “warned”; NASB supplies “escape” and “who warns.”
NASB follows the critical text (“I will shake”); “at that time” is rendered “then.”
“Signifies” is rendered “denotes”; NASB adds “expression.”
“Have grace” is rendered “show gratitude,” and “serve well pleasingly” “offer … an acceptable service”; NASB follows the critical text (“reverence and awe”).
NASB omits “also.”
